//: Seeded into the container's VS Code user-data dir (User/ and Machine/) at session start.
//KNOWN-ISSUE: These do NOT currently affect the workbench UI. openvscode-server web resolves workbench settings from the BROWSER's IndexedDB, not from the server's user-data-dir. Verified failing on clean browser state via all three server-side levers: User/settings.json, Machine/settings.json, and product.json configurationDefaults. The remaining viable fix is to seed browser storage before the workbench boots (our proxy already fronts the IDE, so it can inject a pre-boot script). Until then the candidate sees a Workspace Trust modal and VS Code's own Chat panel. Left in place because this is the correct home for these settings once that lever lands, and because they do reach the remote extension host.
//trust: Candidate is otherwise greeted by a modal security dialog and the window drops into Restricted Mode. Every problem repo is generated by us into a disposable container, so there is no trust decision for them to make. NOTE: this setting alone never stopped the modal — the working lever is the top-level enableWorkspaceTrust boot option forced by workbench-inject.ts; kept for the extension host.
//spoilers: QA 2026-08-14, three live rounds: problem.json (planted bug file+line and the full grading rubric) plus pipeline marker files were sitting in the candidate's Explorer and quick-open. The panes surface refuses to list or serve these (session.ts /api/files, /api/file); the IDE gets the same contract via exclude defaults. A terminal `cat` can still reach them — spoiler-proofing for honest practice, not a security boundary.
//chat: VS Code's built-in Chat sits in the secondary side bar and captures typing. Observed in browser testing: text intended for the editor landed in VS Code's chat box instead, where we cannot see it — same silent-data-loss shape as the terminal.
//agentmode: An interview round has no legitimate use for an AI assistant — this is the one product where the assistant is the thing being tested against. These keys exist in this build (openvscode-server 1.105.1, verified by grepping the workbench bundle) and are kept because they are semantically correct. THEY DO NOT HIDE THE CHAT PANEL: verified live 2026-08-19 with all three delivered via configurationDefaults (confirmed present in the injected boot HTML), the Chat view still auto-opened in the auxiliary bar — 191px on first boot, 300px after a reload. The auxiliary bar is driven by PERSISTED VIEW STATE, not by settings: vscode-web-state-db-global > ItemTable > workbench.panel.chat.hidden holds [{id:workbench.panel.chat.view.copilot,isHidden:false}]. Seeding that key before boot is the real lever — the same browser-storage channel the KNOWN-ISSUE above named. CSS is not a substitute: display:none on .part.auxiliarybar leaves a 191px dead gap because the editor part width is JS-driven.
//noise: The round starts on the problem, not on a Welcome tab or a tip.
//quiet: No update prompts or telemetry inside a timed interview round.
//editor: Deterministic editing surface: no AI autocomplete during an interview.
//recommendations: QA ISSUE-009: a stock 'install the Python extension?' modal popped mid-interview.
//theme: Graphite Steel re-skin: pull the workbench onto the shell's palette (bg #0e0e0f, sunk #131314, steel #35708f for position/focus) so the embedded editor doesn't read as a third, unowned skin. Reaches the workbench via injectWorkbenchDefaults (workbench-inject.ts) — the //KNOWN-ISSUE above predates that lever.
